rounds.restatement: In the template resolver's TABLE rendering, a cell value that contains a pipe or a newline currently breaks the markdown table. The fix must escape each pipe as \| and turn each newline (LF or CRLF) into one space. This applies to header cells and body cells, in static ROWs and in ROWs generated by FOR. Nothing outside table cells may change, no existing test may be edited, and no runtime dependency may be added. The change serves the cycle goal of fixing the Tier 0 bugs in a deterministic core library.

findings.title: Unconditional pipe escaping double-escapes escape_md output inside table cells and splits the row again

serves.scenario: Before this change, a template author could make a pipe safe in a cell by writing ${{a|escape_md}}, because escape_md backslash-escapes '|'. The cell rendered as 'x\|y' and the table kept its column count. Now processCellsArray escapes every '|' again, so the cell becomes 'x\\|y'. GFM parses the '\\' as an escaped backslash, so the '|' that follows is a live column delimiter and the row gains an extra column. The fix changes behavior outside the named defect and breaks the very case c1 protects (the row keeps its column count) for already-escaped input.

findings.rubric: c1: a pipe inside a cell is escaped so the row keeps its column count; m1: change behavior outside the named defects
findings.reproduction: resolveTemplate('{{TABLE}}{{ROW}}${{a|escape_md}}|z{{END_ROW}}{{END_TABLE}}', new Map([['a','x|y']]), {strictMode:false}). Before the fix this gives '| x\|y | z |' (two columns in GFM). After the fix it gives '| x\\|y | z |', which a GFM renderer splits into three cells ('x\', 'y', 'z'). Smallest fix: escape only pipes that are not already preceded by a backslash, for example content.replace(/\r?\n/g, ' ').replace(/(^|[^\\])\|/g, '$1\\|'), applied repeatedly or with a lookbehind (?<!\\)\|. Alternatively, have escape_md and cell escaping agree on a single escaping step.
findings.label: f1

rulings.note: valid: already escaped pipes from escape_md must not be escaped twice
